description:
Nightwing provides technically advanced full-spectrum cyber, data operations, systems integration and intelligence mission support services to meet our customers’ most demanding challenges. Our capabilities include cyber space operations, cyber defense and resiliency, vulnerability research, ubiquitous technical surveillance, data intelligence, lifecycle mission enablement, and software modernization. Nightwing brings disruptive technologies, agility, and competitive offerings to customers in the intelligence community, defense, civil, and commercial markets.
 
 Software Developer I (System Security) 
 Join Nightwing's Products team and work at the cutting edge of multi-layered cyber resiliency solutions protecting mission-critical systems. Our software-based cyber resiliency solutions have been field-deployed since 2009, protecting the confidentiality and integrity of data and applications on Department of Defense weapon systems and platforms. Our threat model assumes adversaries have gained escalated privileges and bypassed traditional security controls—we build the last line of defense.
  
 We're seeking an entry level software developer to strengthen our flagship security products, which provide deep OS-level protections for Windows, Linux, and VxWorks environments. You'll develop security capabilities that lock down execution environments, protect applications and data at rest and during execution, and implement robust cyber detection and response mechanisms.
  
 This role is ideal for an early career software developer who wants to dive deep into operating system internals and low-level security engineering. While you don't need to be a kernel developer today, you should be excited about becoming one and have the foundation to get there quickly.
  
 Security Clearance: 
 Must meet the requirements to obtain and maintain a Secret government security clearance 

 U.S. Citizenship is required. Qualified applicants may be subject to a security investigation and must meet minimum qualifications for access to classified information.
  
 Required Qualifications: 
 Academic and/or internship experience in software development 
 C/C++ skills with a basic understanding of memory management, pointers, and low-level programming concepts
 Familiarity with software/hardware debugging 
 Version control familiarity (Git)
 Ability to learn new technical concepts 
   
 Typically requires: 
 A University Degree in STEM such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, etc.
  
 What Sets Qualified Candidates Apart: 
 You don't need all of these, but strong candidates typically have one or more:
 Understanding of operating system concepts: process/thread management, memory management, I/O systems, interrupt handling
 Assembly language experience (x86_64, ARM) - reading and debugging at the instruction level
 Experience with scripting languages (Python, Batch) for automation and testing
 Familiarity with security concepts: cryptography, threat modeling, attack surfaces
  
 What You'll Work On: 
 Developing and enhancing OS-level security features that operate deep within the operating system
 Building detection and response mechanisms to counter advanced persistent threats
 Implementing cryptographic binding of sensitive software to trusted hardware
 Integrating with Hardware Root of Trust (HRoT) solutions
 Protecting against sophisticated attacks from well-funded adversaries
 Supporting multi-OS platforms (Windows, Linux, VxWorks)
 Learning kernel programming and driver development on the job with mentorship from our senior engineers
  
 Our Ideal Candidate: 
 You're a strong programmer who gets excited about understanding how things work at the lowest levels. You're comfortable reading documentation, source code, and assembly when needed. You know what you don’t know and are comfortable seeking mentorship. You're energized by deep technical challenges. You understand that security is an adversarial discipline and you're ready to think like both builder and attacker.
  
 Why Join Our Team: 
 Work on technology protecting critical DoW weapon systems and platforms
 Learn from senior engineers with over 15 years of experience in mission-critical system protection
 Grow your expertise in Linux/Windows internals, kernel development, and low-level security
 Contribute to a multi-layered cyber resiliency portfolio that spans hardware, firmware, software, and network layers
 See the direct impact of your work on national security
 Access to cutting-edge tools, training, and technologies
 Recognition for exceptional results
 
Previously part of a leading Fortune 100 company and headquartered in Dulles, VA; Nightwing became independent in 2024 but continues to support the nation’s most mission impactful initiatives.
  
 When we formed Nightwing, we brought a deep set of credentials and an unfaltering commitment to the mission. For over four decades, our team has been providing some of the world’s most technically advanced full-spectrum cyber, data operations, systems integration and intelligence support services to the U.S. government on its most important missions.
  
 At Nightwing, we value collaboration and teamwork. You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside talented individuals who are passionate about what they do. Together, we’ll leverage our collective expertise to drive innovation, solve complex problems, and deliver exceptional results for our clients.
  
 Thank you for considering joining us as we embark on this new journey and shape the future of cybersecurity and intelligence together as part of the Nightwing team.
